title: From Engineered Features to Foundation Models: A Decade of Teaching Machines to See, Told Through One Research Path
content: Many of the questions computer vision asked in 2017 are still being asked today. Can a machine understand a scene the way a person does? Can it find a tumor in a tissue sample? Can it tell who someone is from the way they move or read? The core questions are familiar, but the way we answer them has changed almost completely, and in the process some of the questions have grown. This paper tells that story through one line of research that started in the era of hand-built features and early deep networks and continues into the era of foundation models and AI agents. We walk through what we built then, what we build now, and what changed in between. We describe six shifts in plain terms: where a model's knowledge comes from, how much labeled data it needs, how it handles context, how it combines different kinds of signals, how it is adapted to a new task, and what it finally produces. We close with the questions that did not go away, and that matter more now than before.
